On October 30, 2026, in connection with the Kenvue Acquisition, our Board of Directors approved the Kenvue Integration Program (the "Program") which is intended to achieve certain operating profit synergies by 2030.

The Program is expected to result in cumulative pre-tax charges of approximately $3.1 billion ($2.5 billion cash and $0.6 billion non-cash) over this period, with cash charges primarily related to supply chain network optimization (approximately $800), enterprise resource planning and technology integration (approximately $600), workforce optimization (approximately $400), advisory services (approximately $400)…
The transformation is expected to impact our organization in all major geographies, and workforce reductions are expected to be in the range of 4% to 5%.
We anticipate that full year capital spending will be approximately $1.3 billion, including incremental spending from the 2024 Transformation Initiative.

The aggregate principal amount of Kenvue Notes that remained outstanding following the settlement of the exchange offers was approximately $0.6 billion and will be reflected in our consolidated total debt following the acquisition.

Further, we do not expect restrictions or taxes on repatriation of cash held outside of the U.S. to have a material effect on our overall business, liquidity, financial condition or results of operations for the foreseeable future.
There can be no assurance that these future events will occur as anticipated or that our results will be as estimated.

• 2024 Transformation Initiative - We initiated this transformation to create a more agile and focused operating structure that will accelerate our proprietary pipeline of innovation in right-to-win spaces and improve our growth trajectory, profitability, and returns on investment.

• IFP Repatriated Earnings - In connection with the IFP Transaction, we recognized deferred tax liabilities for certain permanently reinvested earnings from the IFP Business that are expected to be repatriated.

We may encounter difficulties integrating our and Kenvue’s businesses and operations and, therefore, may fail to realize the projected benefits and cost savings of the Kenvue Acquisition, which could adversely affect the value of our common stock.

The success of the combined company will depend, in part, on our ability to realize the anticipated benefits and cost savings from combining K-C’s and Kenvue’s respective businesses, including operational and other synergies that we believe the combined company will be able to achieve.

The anticipated benefits and cost savings of the Kenvue Acquisition may not be realized fully or at all, may take longer to realize than expected or could have other adverse effects that we do not currently foresee.

If we are unable to successfully combine the businesses in an efficient, cost-effective manner within the anticipated timeframe, the projected benefits and cost savings may not be realized fully or may take longer to realize than expected and our business may be unable to grow as planned, which could materially impact our business, cash flow, financial condition or results of operations as well as adversely…

We expect to continue to incur substantial non-recurring costs in connection with integrating the operations of K-C and Kenvue, including costs to replace services and manufacturing that Kenvue currently receives from Johnson & Johnson ("J&J") under transitional arrangements.
Both of these factors could reduce our financial flexibility to continue capital investments, develop new products and declare future dividends.
Events outside our control, including changes in regulation and laws as well as economic trends, also could adversely affect our ability to realize the expected benefits from this acquisition.

For example, regulators including the Federal Drug Administration ("FDA") and the European Medicines Agency have issued guidance on assessing and controlling nitrosamine impurities in medicines, and we are reviewing Kenvue’s product portfolio under that guidance.
We continue to receive information with respect to potential costs and the anticipated number of cases.
